tables.name: prod
tables.label: Production
tables.description: The build the PRODUCTION site is serving right now. Fetched live from devisant.com/isa/build_info.json on every Refresh (mode: replace, so a refresh overwrites rather than accumulates). Seeded empty and never hand-edited — a build stamp is only ever what a real site returned.

tables.name: dev
tables.label: Dev
tables.description: The build the DEV site is serving right now. Fetched live from dev.devisant.com/isa/build_info.json on every Refresh (mode: replace). Seeded empty for the same reason as prod.

tables.name: apkProd
tables.label: Android download (production)
tables.description: The Android APK a new download gets today: the LATEST published (non-prerelease) GitHub release of isa-kit/isan-releases. Its tag is a production build stamp, so it can be read straight against the production site's commit — a native download is cut from a production promote and may sit one promote behind the site. Fetched from the public GitHub REST API on Refresh (mode: replace), unauthenticated, read-only.

tables.name: macProd
tables.label: macOS download (production)
tables.description: The macOS app a new download gets today: the LATEST published (non-prerelease) GitHub release of isa-kit/isan-web, the repo kIsanMacDownloadUrl resolves against. Same production-tag story as apkProd. Fetched from the public GitHub REST API on Refresh (mode: replace).

tables.name: apkDev
tables.label: Android build (dev channel)
tables.description: Assets on the ROLLING dev-latest prerelease tag of isa-kit/isan-releases. This table holds the tag's ASSETS, not the tag itself, on purpose: dev-latest is force-moved in place, so the release's own published_at is when the tag was first created and says nothing about freshness — each asset's own updated_at and its build-stamped filename do. Empty means no dev APK is currently published. Fetched from the public GitHub REST API on Refresh (mode: replace).

tables.name: macDev
tables.label: macOS build (dev channel)
tables.description: Assets on the dev-latest prerelease tag of isa-kit/isan-web, if one exists. Same rolling-tag reasoning as apkDev. This table is EXPECTED to be empty much of the time — the dev channel does not always carry a macOS build — and an empty table here is a real answer, not a failed fetch. Fetched from the public GitHub REST API on Refresh (mode: replace).

tables.name: appsProd
tables.label: Applets on production
tables.description: Every applet the PRODUCTION web build actually ships, with the seedVersion that build carries. Fetched from devisant.com/isa/versions.json (the manifest tool/write_versions.py writes next to build_info.json on every deploy) into.path applets, mode replace. A devOnly applet is omitted from the prod manifest by the generator, matching the pruned artifact — so an applet present in appsDev and missing here has not been promoted.

tables.name: appsDev
tables.label: Applets on dev
tables.description: Every applet the DEV web build ships, with its seedVersion, from dev.devisant.com/isa/versions.json into.path applets, mode replace. The dev manifest keeps devOnly applets. Seeded empty like every other table here.
